subject: Egress ownership & firewall namespaces — runbook and SLA check
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@novacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Private endpoint egress requirements and evidence request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the NovaCorp security and infra teams had a few follow-up asks before we can move the private deployment to procurement:  

- We need a single canonical list of egress IPs and port ranges to allow from our perimeter firewall for both the runtime data-plane and the control-plane (if any).
- If any of the IPs are shared/ephemeral across customers, we need the rotation cadence and a mitigation plan.
- What TLS termination will Redwood perform? We need to know whether outbound traffic requires FQDN-based allowlisting or fixed IPs (SNI/TLS inspection implications).
- Audit evidence: sample Syslog/Netflow records or a short packet-capture showing a successful call from a private endpoint to your control plane.
- Minimum acceptable SLA window for outbound connectivity and any fallback behavior if the control plane is unreachable.

Can you provide the above (or a runbook) so we can sign off on firewall rules? Procurement also asked us to get anything in writing we can attach to the purchase order.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Jenkins
Director, Cloud Security
NovaCorp

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements and evidence request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a compact runbook and an IP matrix (attached) that addresses each ask; top-level notes below. Attaching: egress-ip-matrix.csv, private-deploy-runbook-v0.9.pdf.

Summary (high level):
- Split model: we treat runtime (data-plane) outbound separately from control-plane telemetry/orchestration. For Private (VPC) deployments we support two flavors:
  1) Data-plane via customer-managed NAT: runtime outbound uses your per-tenant NAT IPs (recommended for maximal tenancy isolation). In that case Redwood doesn't require static outbound egress from your NATs to our control plane except for management flows listed below.
  2) Redwood-managed egress gateway: if you prefer Redwood to provide a dedicated egress IP set, we assign a small CIDR of stable IPs (listed in the CSV).

- Control-plane endpoints (registration, model-pull, health-checks): we require allowlist entries to the following hostnames/IPs (see CSV). These are stable for the next 12 months; if rotation is required we will provide a 30‑day notice plus a rotation cadence and signed attestation.

- Ports and protocols: outbound TCP 443 is the only protocol required for control-plane and most external model pulls. Optional telemetry (syslog/metrics) can use TCP 6514 (syslog-TLS) or HTTPS POST to your collector; see runbook. Data-plane model inference connections may open additional ephemeral outbound flows if you enable remote integrations (e.g., external KB or S3 retrieval), and those are documented per-integration in the runbook.

- TLS/SNI guidance: Redwood keeps end-to-end TLS for customer model requests. For control-plane interactions we use mTLS (mutual TLS) to our control-plane endpoints; therefore customer firewalls must allow outbound SNI for hostname resolution but do not need to perform TLS termination for redundancy. If your policy requires TLS inspection, our recommendation is to allowlist IPs + hostnames to avoid breaking mTLS.

- Evidence and observability: Attached runbook includes an example Syslog snippet and a sample NetFlow export showing a successful control-plane handshake. If you want a live demonstration we can generate a short, one-off PCAP and provide a signed artifact for PO attachment.

Action items I propose:
1) Review the attached CSV and confirm whether you prefer customer NAT or Redwood-managed egress.
2) If customer NAT, confirm the public IPs we should expect. If Redwood-managed, sign the SLA addendum for stable egress IPs (I can send DocuSign).
3) For audit attachments — tell me whether a PCAP + signed note or syslog sample is preferred and we will provide it.

Looping in David and Kimberly internally to confirm observability hooks and runbook completion.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress ownership & firewall namespaces — runbook and SLA check

Mina — quick additions for the runbook before we send to NovaCorp: 

- Observability hooks: we should require (and document) one of the following ingestion endpoints on the customer side for acceptance testing:
  * Syslog-TLS (TCP 6514) endpoint that we post an initial handshake event to; OR
  * HTTPS endpoint (Bearer token) for NetFlow/metrics JSON POSTs.
  This allows us to provide live evidence (and reduces need for PCAP).

- Per-tenant NAT guidance: call out the security tradeoffs explicitly. Per-tenant NAT = best isolation; shared NAT + CIDR = easier ops but requires tight audit windows. Add a short table in the runbook summarizing when we recommend each option (prod vs dev vs regulated).

- Fallback behavior: document that if control-plane is unreachable we keep inference running on pinned model weights for up to X minutes (configurable), and then degrade to read-only or a cached-outputs mode depending on tenant policy. We need acceptance from Nova on the timeout default (we usually propose 15 mins).

Kimberly — can you confirm encryption/KMS notes for the runbook? Specifically whether we should mandate HSM-backed keys for customers requiring FIPS-level attestation.

Thanks,
David

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T18:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress ownership & firewall namespaces — runbook and SLA check

Adding a couple of items for NovaCorp's runbook:

- KMS/HSM: For customers that flag FIPS/HIPAA requirements we must offer the option to use HSM-backed keys for model signing and control-plane mTLS certs. Call this out in a short appendix with the integration steps and the expected timeline for HSM onboarding (typically 4–6 weeks).

- Signed attestation: include an attestation template indicating the egress IPs we guarantee for 12 months, plus the rotation cadence if Redwood-managed egress is requested. We should attach that template as a separate PDF.

- Audit retention: confirm the retention window for the supplied Syslog sample (we will keep PoC artifacts for 90 days; if they need longer we can add an addendum).

Proposed edits to the runbook are in the Drive link. Mina — if you send the DocuSign, I can attach the attestation template and we should be good to go.

— Kimberly

From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@novacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements and evidence request

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. We prefer customer-managed per-tenant NAT for production; we'll share the public IPs by EOD Monday. For the audit evidence, a signed syslog snippet and the attestation PDF is sufficient for procurement.

Please send the DocuSign for the SLA addendum and the attestation template you mentioned. Also confirm the default control-plane failover timeout (you suggested 15 mins) and we'll either accept or counter-propose in the PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Alice
